items.front: Fundamental Duties — Part, Article, and how added?
items.back: Part IV-A, single Article 51A; added by the 42nd Amendment (1976). Not in the original 1950 Constitution.

items.front: On whose recommendation were Fundamental Duties added, and inspired by which country?
items.back: Swaran Singh Committee (1976); inspired by the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR.

items.front: How many duties originally, and how many now?
items.back: Originally 10; the 86th Amendment (2002) added the 11th (parent/guardian to provide education, ages 6-14).
items.examPoint: 86th Amendment Act 2002 added the 11th duty (education, ages 6-14)

items.front: Are Fundamental Duties enforceable by a court?
items.back: No — they are non-justiciable; but Parliament may prescribe penalties by law, and courts use them to interpret statutes.

items.front: To whom do Fundamental Duties apply?
items.back: Only to citizens of India — not to foreigners or the State.
items.examPoint: Applicable to citizens only (not to all persons/foreigners)

items.front: 'To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India' is which provision?
items.examPoint: Duties (b)-(d) — freedom-struggle ideals, sovereignty/unity/integrity, defence & national service

items.front: In India, what is the relationship between rights and duties?
items.back: Rights are correlative with duties — the two go together.
items.examPoint: Significance — balancing rights with responsibilities & civic sense

items.front: Which single duty mentions the dignity of women?
items.back: 51A(e) — promote harmony and renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women.
items.examPoint: Duty 51A(e) — common brotherhood & renouncing practices derogatory to women

items.front: Which duty covers scientific temper, and which covers the environment?
items.back: 51A(h) = scientific temper, humanism, spirit of inquiry; 51A(g) = protect the natural environment.
items.examPoint: Duties (h)-(j) — scientific temper, safeguard public property/abjure violence, strive for excellence

items.front: Which committee (1999) reviewed operationalising Fundamental Duties?
items.examPoint: Verma Committee (1999) on operationalisation of duties

items.front: Besides FRs, which parts reflect the UDHR 1948?
items.examPoint: Complementary to DPSP (Part IV) & Fundamental Rights (Part III)

items.front: Which case linked the National Anthem to duty 51A(a)?
items.back: Shyam Narayan Chouksey v. Union of India (2016) — anthem in cinemas; order relaxed/modified in 2018.
items.examPoint: Shyam Narayan Chouksey v. Union of India — National Anthem case (2016/2018)
